correctness.rationale: Any tree has precisely one size-b-part spoke with two edges (otherwise disconnected if none, four-cycle if at least two); the remaining b-1 spokes choose one of two attachments independently. This is a bijection giving b2^(b-1) trees. For independent trees equal bridge spokes have probability 1/b, with intersection 2+Bin(b-1,1/2); unequal bridges yield 2+Bin(b-2,1/2). Thus X=law 2+Bin(b-2,1/2)+Bern(1/(2b)) independently, support [2,b+1], mean (b+1)²/(2b), variance (b-1)(b²-b+1)/(4b²). Binomial unimodality and the convolution difference give exact total variation p*binom(b-2,floor((b-2)/2))/2^(b-2) with p=1/(2b). Fresh all-pairs exact rational enumeration b=2..6 agreed. The bridge-spoke bijection proves arbitrary b.
